steps.question: What is each sample's 20-gene signature score, computed consistently for all 120 samples (60 cases, 60 controls) from the raw Salmon gene counts in counts.csv?

steps.description: Load counts.csv (12,000 genes x 120 samples) and metadata.csv (condition, time, event), reconcile sample IDs between the two, then apply DESeq2-style normalization (median-of-ratios size factors via pydeseq2) and a variance-stabilizing transform. Compute the primary per-sample signature score as the mean z-scored VST log-expression across the 20 genes in signature_genes.csv, and a secondary rank-based score (singscore-style mean rank above background) to guard against length-correction and scale artifacts — the data profile notes Salmon length correction is unconfirmed, so the rank-based score is the sensitivity anchor. Output: scores.csv (sample_id, score_primary, score_rank, condition, time, event) plus a QC summary (size factors, signature-gene overlap, per-condition score summaries). Caveat to record: no clinical covariates exist in the metadata and the cohort is a single batch, so no further adjustment or batch correction is possible or needed.
acceptance_criteria: A sample-level table with exactly 120 rows joined on sample IDs, carrying condition, time, event, and at least two signature scores (primary VST z-mean score, secondary rank-based score)
Explicit report of how many of the 20 signature genes are present in the 12,000-gene matrix, with missing genes named (not silently dropped)
Library-size / size-factor summary and per-condition score distribution (median, IQR) recorded
If fewer than 15 of the 20 genes are found, the step reports this as a blocking caveat rather than proceeding on a degenerate score

steps.name: Cox models for score vs time-to-event
caveats: Assert the event coding (1 = event, 0 = censored) and the time units from metadata before fitting; a flipped event column silently inverts every hazard ratio
With 60/60 unpaired samples the effective event count may be small in one stratum; prefer the pooled adjusted model as primary and treat stratum-specific HRs as descriptive
If the PH test rejects for the score, report a time-varying or split-time sensitivity check rather than presenting the global HR as final
steps.question: In the 120-sample cohort, does the signature score associate with time-to-event after adjusting for condition (case vs control), and does that association differ between cases and controls?
constraints: Primary analysis uses the continuous standardized score; do not dichotomize in the primary model
Fit models with lifelines CoxPHFitter (or scikit-survival CoxPHFitter) — not a linear model on log-time
Report both the condition-adjusted HR and the crude (score-only) HR so the effect of adjustment is visible
steps.description: Fit Cox proportional-hazards models on the 120-sample score table from T1S1: (a) primary adjusted model with standardized primary score + condition; (b) interaction model score + condition + score x condition with a likelihood-ratio test of the interaction, to answer whether the score's association with time-to-event is present overall and whether it differs between cases and controls; (c) stratified secondary fits (score within cases only, within controls only) for interpretability. Check the proportional-hazards assumption with Schoenfeld residuals (lifelines proportional_hazard_test), report Harrell's C-index (scikit-survival concordance_index_censored) with a bootstrap or cross-validated C-index for the score alone. The 20-gene signature is pre-specified — no feature selection is performed inside or outside resampling — so the reported associations carry no selection optimism; state this explicitly in the output. Report the time and event variables as delivered (units and event coding asserted from metadata before fitting).
acceptance_criteria: Primary Cox model (score + condition) fitted with HR, 95% CI, Wald and likelihood-ratio p-values for the score reported
Interaction model (score * condition) fitted with a likelihood-ratio test of the interaction term reported, distinguishing prognostic (main effect) from predictive (interaction) association
Schoenfeld-residual PH test per covariate and the model concordance index reported
Per-stratum event counts (cases and controls) reported; if any stratum has <10 events, the stratum-specific estimate is flagged as unstable rather than silently omitted
All coefficients written to a results table with model formula, n, number of events, and convergence status

steps.name: Robustness checks and survival visualization
caveats: Tertiles in a 60-sample stratum give ~20 samples per group — wide KM curves; report confidence intervals and treat log-rank p-values near 0.05 as inconclusive
Do not iterate leave-one-gene-out into a selection exercise; it is a stability diagnostic, and no gene is removed from the reported signature
steps.question: Are the score-outcome associations from T2S1 robust to scoring method, discretization, and the choice of individual signature genes, in cases and in controls separately?
constraints: Use the same event/time coding and sample set as T2S1 — no sample dropping between steps
Keep the primary continuous-score model as the headline result; tertile KM and log-rank are supportive visualization, not the primary test
steps.description: Stress-test the T2S1 result: (a) Kaplan-Meier estimates and log-rank tests by score tertiles, computed separately within the 60 cases and within the 60 controls so the continuous-model finding has a visible, non-parametric counterpart; (b) leave-one-gene-out stability — recompute the score dropping each signature gene in turn and refit the primary adjusted model, summarizing the spread of HRs and p-values; (c) repeat the primary model with the secondary rank-based score from T1S1 to confirm the association is not an artifact of the VST z-mean scoring; (d) produce publication-grade figures: KM curves by tertile within each condition, and a forest plot of the primary, interaction, and sensitivity HRs. Close with a one-paragraph verdict stating whether the score's association with time-to-event, adjusted for condition, survives all checks.
acceptance_criteria: Kaplan-Meier curves by score tertile fitted separately within cases and within controls, each with a log-rank p-value

Leave-one-gene-out analysis over the 20 signature genes reporting the range of adjusted HRs (or at minimum the range of score coefficients and p-values) and naming any gene whose removal changes the qualitative conclusion
Secondary (rank-based) score fitted in the primary Cox specification with its HR and p-value alongside the primary score's, with an explicit statement of which conclusions are method-robust
Figures and a short robustness table saved as outputs

plan.title: 20-gene signature score vs time-to-event in case-control cohort
plan.analytical_narrative: The cohort is 120 human tumor biopsies (60 cases vs 60 controls, unpaired, single batch) with raw Salmon gene-level counts for 12,000 genes, a 4-column metadata table (condition, time, event), and a pre-specified 20-gene signature. The question is prognostic/predictive: does the signature score associate with time-to-event after accounting for case vs control status? Plan: (1) normalize the raw counts (DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors + variance-stabilizing transform, since the profile flags that Salmon length correction is unconfirmed) and compute a per-sample signature score with a primary continuous method (mean z-scored VST log-expression of the 20 genes) and a rank-based secondary method, explicitly reconciling sample IDs and reporting signature-gene overlap with the 12,000-gene matrix; (2) fit Cox proportional-hazards models — score + condition as the primary adjusted model, plus a score-by-condition interaction model to test whether the association differs between cases and controls — with PH-assumption checks and concordance; (3) run robustness checks (score tertiles with Kaplan-Meier/log-rank within cases and within controls, leave-one-gene-out stability, secondary scoring method) because the score drives the result only if these agree. The signature is fixed a priori, so no feature selection occurs and the reported hazard ratios carry no selection optimism; no covariates beyond condition exist in the metadata (single batch), which the report must state as a limitation.
